newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen firm on steady Japanese rates.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen firm on steady Japanese rates.

text.p: The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) accommodative money operations lifted SIMEX euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Wednesday as lingering fears of rate hikes faded, dealers said.
They said BOJ's injection of about 100 billion yen in the morning which left close to 400 billion yen surplus in the market, signalled its commitment to keep rates steady in Japan.
After rising to a high of 98.96, the benchmark March euroyen futures were trading around 98.92 at 1115 GMT, unchanged against its IMM close.
Activity was limited as players awaited the outcome of the two-day Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting ending late Wednesday.

"I don't expect euroyen to move much from current levels. It should be range-bound with resistance at 98.95/96 since a steady rate policy has already been factored in at these levels," a dealer with a European institution said.
A shift in investors' interest to bonds away from equities, BOJ's generous money operations along with an outright bond purchase by Japan's ministry of finance helped underpin JGBs.
"The underlying support for JGBs is strong. There was some strong buying after the Nikkei slumped below 20,000 level," another dealer with a local bank said.
September JGBs ended up 0.09 at 124.58. Volume was a light 510 lots.
Eurodollars futures were mostly steady around their previous IMM setlements ahead of the FOMC meeting and the employment data on Thursday.
March eurodollar futures ended at 93.860 against its IMM close at 93.855. Decmber was at 93.955 against 93.950 previously.
